title: V/H/S
review: There's a lot of these asshole young white dudes in the framing segment, and then when the first self-contained segment starts, it's just a different group of asshole young white dudes. So it's quite hard work to watch, with lots of drunken shouting as filler content, before anything horrory happens. Then you have to deal with the original guys again at the transition, and then there's a another segment about an asshole young white dude. It's like a sexual assault themed anthology, and maybe that's intentional and we're meant to see these people get their comeuppance, but it doesn't lean into that and it's just not very imaginative or diverse. Newer {V/H/S} seem so much more frantic and fast, and any anthology needs to have variation to justify itself. Here it's kind of slow and repetitive. What if young white Americans went on a trip, and one of them was an obnoxious guy who likes to shove his camcorder in his friends faces? What if the guys wanted to score some beer and see some boobs, but then they get killed one by one, and the camcorder guy screams and shakes it around a lot? The camcorder drops on the ground at just the right angle to see the last victim die. Repeat five times. At least it ended with the best segment, but if that was in {V/H/S 99} it might have been the worst.
